title: My, your, his, our, their: six endings

sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Hungarian puts the owner on the noun as an ending. There is no separate word for "his" or "her": *kulcsa* means both. After a consonant, *-m* and *-d* need a linking vowel: *kulcs* becomes *kulcsom*, *kulcsod*; the third person adds *-a/-e* or *-ja/-je*, and the word decides: *kulcsa*, but *telefonja*. Several owners: *kulcsunk* (our), *kulcsotok* (your, plural), *kulcsuk* (their). Words that end in *a* lengthen it (and *e* → *é*): *szoba* becomes *szobám*, *szobánk*.

items.spanish: Anna itt van. A táskája nagy.
items.english: Anna is here. Her bag is big.

sections.content: Small letters change the owner: *barátunk* is our friend, *barátjuk* is their friend. And *szobád* is for one person, *szobátok* for several.
